title: Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading (Eliseev, Mazur)
setup: Mixtral-8x7B (46.7B, 8 experts, top-2); HQQ 4-bit attn, 2/3-bit experts (2-bit ~2.6 bpw); T4 Colab, RTX 3080 Mobile, RTX 3060, A100 reference; LRU k=2 (3060) or 4; batch 1; experts in host RAM over PCIe

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 66.66 = FP16 attn + 2-bit experts (19.33 GB); 4-bit attn + 2-bit = 65.58 (17.54 GB)

why: GPU, PCIe host RAM, 8 big experts, cache is 25-50% of experts; byte lever (2.6 bpw) same as ours, LRU gain not transferable at 2-8 footprint caches over 512 experts
limitations: Speculative prediction future work; PCIe-bound 2-4 tok/s

title: VPTQ: Extreme Low-bit Vector Post-Training Quantization for LLMs (Liu et al., EMNLP 2024)
setup: LLaMA-2 7/13/70B, LLaMA-3, Mistral-7B dense; quantised on 4xA100, fine-tune 8xH100; tok/s on GPU not named, naive torch/Triton kernels, 256 generated tokens

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: unchecked item in PyPI Road Map

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: first-pass: PyPI page failed to load

why: GPU kernels, dense models, Hessian weighting plus fine-tuning, about 2 bit not 1 bit; no MoE
ablation: Yes: vector length / codebook size / RVQ / outliers / fine-tune (Tables 10-11); closest cell v=4,k=256
limitations: Could not fine-tune 70B long; English only
contradicts_our_findings: No; supports refutation of 1.3 bpw: even Hessian-weighted v=4,k=256 at 2 bit is ppl 7.21 vs 4.57

title: GPTVQ: The Blessing of Dimensionality for LLM Quantization (van Baalen et al., Qualcomm)
id_read: arXiv 2402.15319v1 and v2 (v2 re-framed for mobile CPU)
setup: Llama-1/2/3, Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x7B; WikiText2 calib; v2 Table 1 Snapdragon X Elite, Llama-3-8B, own C engine, batch 1; baselines llama.cpp Q4_0, own INT4 g128

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: better size/accuracy than scalar, Llama-2 and Mistral, 2-3 bits
first-pass: VQ better latency than INT4 on mobile CPU

why: Only CPU LUT evidence, but 3.1 bpv, indices <=6 bit, DRAM-bound mobile SoC, Hessian calibration; not NVMe-bound, not 1 bpw
ablation: v1 Tables 6-11 (EM init, codebook fine-tune, scaling)
limitations: Small codebooks/low dimension chosen for CPU may cost perplexity vs 8D AQLM
contradicts_our_findings: No; its design rule (index<=6 bit, dim<=4) is opposite of 8-dim 256 words

title: Mixture Compressor for MoE LLMs Gains More (Huang et al., ICLR 2025)
setup: Mixtral-8x7B and 8x22B; compress on 2-4 A100; test A100, RTX 3090; HQQ-based CUDA kernel; baselines GPTQ uniform, BSP, Hessian

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: static expert quantisation plus dynamic pruning below 3 bits

why: 8 experts, GPU resident, speedup largely from fitting 1 GPU vs 2; large quality loss at 2.05 bit; allocation by activation frequency x routing score x reconstruction error is useful
quality_loss: 2.54 bit -3.8 avg, GSM8K -20.6, HumanEval -29.8, MMLU5 -9.4; 2.05 bit -8.0 avg
ablation: Yes: allocation metrics (Fig 5-6), tokens protection, thresholds
contradicts_our_findings: No; quality now measured and unfavourable at 2-bit

title: D2MoE: Dual Routing and Dynamic Scheduling for Efficient On-Device MoE-based LLM Serving (Wang et al., MobiCom 2025)
setup: LLaMA-MoE-3.5B and Mixtral-8x7B (8 experts, top-2); RTX 3060 6GB + i7-11800H + 32GB + 970 EVO 3.5 GB/s; Jetson AGX Orin 64GB; 128 in/128 out, 4-32 requests, GPU memory budget 200-1600 MB; V1 INT2->4, V2 INT5->8; router fine-tune 2-4h

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: low-bit base plus residual steps, token-adaptive bit-width

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: those are V2 (INT5->8); V1 INT2->4 is 4.28 and 15.68

why: SSD+RAM but GPU needed; nested benefit grows with concurrency 4-32; trained bit-width router; no preloading; 8 experts
quality_loss: V1 INT2->4 Mixtral +0.24 ppl, -1.37 zero-shot; LLaMA-MoE +1.13 ppl
limitations: No async multi-request, no expert preloading, not for NPUs
contradicts_our_findings: No; trained V1 quality is the only published figure for the layout that D.md could not measure

title: MatGPTQ (Kleinegger, Crncevic, Alistarh) at the catalog URL; Matryoshka Quantization (Nair et al., Google DeepMind) is the named method
setup: MatGPTQ: Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B dense, RTX A6000, R={3,4,8}; MatQuant: Gemma-2 2B/9B, Mistral-7B, OmniQuant and QAT, TPUv5e

numbers.what: sliced int4 from int8, no co-training

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: MatQuant yes; MatGPTQ trains 3/4/8 only, no 2-bit accuracy

why: dense models, GPU/TPU, training or calibration; speedups vs BF16
quality_loss: int2 MatQuant still 11-16 points below bf16; MatGPTQ 3-bit -8 points
ablation: Loss weighting (MatQuant Tables 4-5), lambda (MatGPTQ Tables 6-7); none on caching
limitations: Native hardware int8/int4 only; MatGPTQ kernels lose to Marlin from batch 16
contradicts_our_findings: No; supports post-hoc nesting being poor

title: GEMQ (Deng et al., ICML 2026) at the catalog URL; DynaExq (Chu et al.) is a separate paper
setup: GEMQ: DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen1.5-MoE, Mixtral-8x7B, H100-80GB, batch 1, HQQ + Triton, baseline PMQ. DynaExq: Qwen3-30B (128 experts), Qwen3-80B (512 experts, Int4), Phi-3.5-MoE, RTX A6000 48GB, batch 1-32, baseline ExpertFlow and static Int4/Int2

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 18 GB is decode memory; MMLU is in the intro and Table 10
those are at 1.5 bit; 2.5 bit is 4.4x/1.44x

why: GPU HBM-resident, H100/A6000, batch up to 32, coarse experts; DynaExq tiers precision inside HBM, not NVMe streaming
quality_loss: GEMQ -7.2 MMLU points at 2.5 bit; DynaExq -0.5 avg vs static Int4 (Qwen3-80B)
ablation: GEMQ router fine-tune and progressive quantisation (Fig 5, Tables 5, 17-21); DynaExq none isolating caching
contradicts_our_findings: D.md says the 7% MMLU drop is not reproduced; it is reported by GEMQ (static allocation) and was simply not tested by us
